017package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
020
021import java.util.function.Consumer;
022
023import org.apache.juneau.bean.mcp.v20260728.ServerCapabilities;
024import org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.BasicMcpSubscriptionBroker;
025import org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.McpSubscriptionBroker;
026
027/**
028 * Binding-owned behavior configuration ("how" a {@code 2026-07-28} MCP endpoint behaves) &mdash; the single
029 * v2-only aggregate consolidating every per-binding tunable {@link McpEndpoint}/{@link McpRestServlet} previously
030 * exposed as six separate hooks: {@code capabilities}, {@code instructions}, {@code cache}, {@code mrtr},
031 * {@code subscriptions}, and {@code subscriptionBroker}.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * <b>Mutable during setup, effectively immutable once published.</b> Same builder-less mutable-setup idiom as
035 * {@link McpCacheConfig}/{@link McpMrtrConfig}/{@link McpSubscriptionsConfig} and the neutral
036 * {@code org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.McpServerConfig} it sits next to: configure fully via the single
037 * {@code createMcpOptions()} (servlet-subclass path) / {@code getMcpOptions()} (mixin path) override, then never
038 * mutate it afterward. The framework memoizes exactly one instance per binding (see {@link McpRestServlet#getMcpOptions()}
039 * and {@link McpEndpoint#getMcpOptions()}), so a request-time reader sees a stable, request-independent snapshot.
040 *
041 * <p>
042 * The three nested configs ({@link #getCache() cache}, {@link #getMrtr() mrtr}, {@link #getSubscriptions()
043 * subscriptions}) are framework-owned instances created once, here, at construction time. Use the
044 * {@link #cache(Consumer)}/{@link #mrtr(Consumer)}/{@link #subscriptions(Consumer)} configure-blocks to mutate
045 * them in place &mdash; callers never {@code new} a replacement nested config, so the "must return a stable
046 * instance" footgun the pre-consolidation hooks warned about cannot recur.
047 *
048 * <h5 class='section'>The subscription broker default:</h5>
049 * <p>
050 * {@link #getSubscriptionBroker()} defaults to <jk>null</jk>, meaning "framework-derived": the binding lazily
051 * derives a {@link BasicMcpSubscriptionBroker} sized from {@link #getSubscriptions()}'s
052 * {@link McpSubscriptionsConfig#getQueueSize() queueSize} the first time a broker is needed, and memoizes that
053 * one derived instance for the lifetime of the binding (a fresh broker per call would silently split live
054 * subscribers and publishers across unrelated registries). Call {@link #setSubscriptionBroker(McpSubscriptionBroker)}
055 * to supply a custom broker instead (for example one shared across multiple bindings on purpose).
056 *
057 * <h5 class='section'>The idleTimeoutMs / heartbeatIntervalMs caveat:</h5>
058 * <p>
059 * When configuring {@link #subscriptions(Consumer)}, keep
060 * {@link McpSubscriptionsConfig#getHeartbeatIntervalMs() heartbeatIntervalMs} below
061 * {@link McpSubscriptionsConfig#getIdleTimeoutMs() idleTimeoutMs} (see that method's Javadoc) &mdash; otherwise
062 * the idle-timeout watchdog can reap a perfectly healthy connection between two heartbeats.
063 *
064 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
065 * <pre>
066 * McpOptions <jv>options</jv> = <jk>new</jk> McpOptions()
067 *     .setInstructions(<js>"Use tool 'echo' to test."</js>)
068 *     .cache(<jv>c</jv> -&gt; <jv>c</jv>.setToolsList(<jk>new</jk> McpCacheHint().setTtlMs(60_000)))
069 *     .subscriptions(<jv>s</jv> -&gt; <jv>s</jv>.setQueueSize(2048));
070 * </pre>
071 */
072@SuppressWarnings({
073   "java:S115" // Constants use UPPER_snakeCase convention (e.g., MSG_consumerMustNotBeNull)
074})
075public class McpOptions {
076
077   // Error message constant (reused across the cache/mrtr/subscriptions/resourceServer configure-blocks below).
078   private static final String MSG_consumerMustNotBeNull = "consumer must not be null";
079
080   private ServerCapabilities capabilities;
081   private String instructions;
082   private McpCacheConfig cache = new McpCacheConfig();
083   private McpMrtrConfig mrtr = new McpMrtrConfig();
084   private McpResourceServerConfig resourceServer = new McpResourceServerConfig();
085   private McpSubscriptionsConfig subscriptions = new McpSubscriptionsConfig();
086   private McpSubscriptionBroker subscriptionBroker;
087
088   @SuppressWarnings({
089      "java:S3077" // Volatile is required for correct double-checked locking in resolveSubscriptionBroker(): unlike a plain lazy read, two BasicMcpSubscriptionBroker instances are NOT equivalent (each holds distinct live per-connection subscription state), so exactly one derived broker must ever be created and published or a subscription registered against one instance would never be visible to a publish call against the other.
090   })
091   private volatile McpSubscriptionBroker derivedBroker;
092
093   private final Object lock = new Object();
094

113    */

157         throw iaex("cache must not be null");

162   /**
163    * Mutates this binding's cache configuration in place.
164    *
165    * <p>
166    * Preferred over {@link #setCache(McpCacheConfig)} for incremental configuration since it operates on the
167    * framework-owned instance rather than requiring the caller to construct a replacement.
168    *
169    * @param consumer Callback invoked with the framework-owned {@link McpCacheConfig}. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
170    * @return This object (for method chaining).
171    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code consumer} is <jk>null</jk>.
172    */
173   public McpOptions cache(Consumer<McpCacheConfig> consumer) {
174      if (consumer == null)
175         throw iaex(MSG_consumerMustNotBeNull);
176      consumer.accept(cache);
177      return this;
178   }

182    *

184    */

187   }
188

195    */
196   public McpOptions setMrtr(McpMrtrConfig value) {

201   }

293   /**
294    * The explicit subscription broker for this binding, if one was supplied.
295    *
296    * @return The explicit broker, or <jk>null</jk> if none was supplied (the default) &mdash; in which case the
297    *    binding lazily derives and memoizes one (see {@link #resolveSubscriptionBroker()}).
298    */
299   public McpSubscriptionBroker getSubscriptionBroker() {
300      return subscriptionBroker;
301   }
302
303   /**
304    * Sets an explicit subscription broker, bypassing the framework-derived default.
305    *
306    * <p>
307    * Setting this after {@link #resolveSubscriptionBroker()} has already derived and published a default
308    * broker for this instance does not retroactively clear or replace that already-published derived
309    * broker &mdash; {@link #resolveSubscriptionBroker()} always prefers an explicit value set here over a
310    * previously-derived one, but under the never-mutate-after-setup contract this method should only be
311    * called during configuration, before the binding is handed to the framework.
312    *
313    * @param value The new value. Can be <jk>null</jk> to revert to the framework-derived default.
314    * @return This object (for method chaining).
315    */
316   public McpOptions setSubscriptionBroker(McpSubscriptionBroker value) {
317      subscriptionBroker = value;
318      return this;
319   }
320
321   /**
322    * Returns {@link #getSubscriptionBroker()} if explicitly set, otherwise lazily derives and memoizes a
323    * {@link BasicMcpSubscriptionBroker} sized from {@link #getSubscriptions()}'s queue bound.
324    *
325    * <p>
326    * This is the <b>effective</b> broker accessor: unlike {@link #getSubscriptionBroker()} (which returns
327    * <jk>null</jk> by default), this method never returns <jk>null</jk>, deriving a default the first time
328    * one is needed. Internal plumbing for {@link McpEndpoint#subscriptionBroker()} /
329    * {@link McpRestServlet#getSubscriptionBroker()}. Since this {@link McpOptions} instance is itself
330    * memoized once per binding, the derived broker this method publishes is likewise stable for the
331    * binding's lifetime &mdash; publication uses double-checked locking (not a plain lazy read) because two
332    * {@link BasicMcpSubscriptionBroker} instances are <b>not</b> equivalent: each holds distinct live
333    * per-connection subscription state, so a benign publication race would silently split subscribers and
334    * publishers across two unrelated registries.
335    *
336    * @return The subscription broker to use. Never <jk>null</jk>.
337    */
338   public McpSubscriptionBroker resolveSubscriptionBroker() {
339      var explicit = subscriptionBroker;
340      if (explicit != null)
341         return explicit;
342      var result = derivedBroker;
343      if (result == null) {
344         synchronized (lock) {
345            result = derivedBroker;
346            if (result == null) {
347               result = new BasicMcpSubscriptionBroker(subscriptions.getQueueSize());
348               derivedBroker = result;
349            }
350         }
351      }
352      return result;
353   }
354}
